newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen mixed to higher after durables data.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen mixed to higher after durables data.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are likely to open mixed to modestly higher Wednesday following yesterday's stunning rally and softer-than-expected durable goods data for May, analysts said.

"Durable goods are down versus an expected rise," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co said. "It shows the first decline in shipments in some time. The economy is holding steady as she goes and the Fed is expected to keep rates on hold. Stocks should open mixed to slightly higher."
Durable goods orders fell 0.6 percent, compared with an revised 1.8 percent increase in April. Economists had forecast a 0.6 percent increase in May.
"This is a weak report," said Sherry Cooper, chief economist at Nesbitt Burns. "Non-defense capital goods orders bounced back but shipments declined."
Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics, said, "From the interest-rate perspective, the data are good. Demand looks cool, which helps restrain inflation."
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was down one point at 904. The long bond was down 12/32 at a 6.72 percent yield.
